newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela starts IMF, World Bank, IDB talks Monday.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela starts IMF, World Bank, IDB talks Monday.

text.p: Venezuela will begin joint talks with the IMF, the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) on Monday about deepening its economic reforms, said central bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez.
He told the International Monetary Fund's policy-making Interim Committee that the country plans to take out an extended fund facility (EFF), three-year loan from the IMF.
"We intend to negotiate a follow-up EFF program with the Fund and will begin joint talks with the Fund, the World Bank and the IDB tomorrow," he said.
"The long-term success of macroeconomic policies can only be guaranted if there are structural reforms to correct root problems," Casas added.
He said Venezuela expects to record a slight fiscal surplus this year, thanks in part to higher oil prices.
In the stand-by loan program worked out between the IMF and Venezuela in April, the country agreed to shoot for a fiscal deficit equivalent to 1.7 percent of gross domestic product this year.
